## What this tracks  
This dataset contains verified 911 emergency service addresses for every location in Nebraska, including street names, numbers, and geographic coordinates.

## Why it matters to you  
When you call 911 from a landline or mobile phone in Nebraska, dispatchers use this data to pinpoint your exact location. Knowing your address is correctly registered helps ensure first responders can find you during emergencies. For businesses, this confirms your official address matches what appears in emergency systems and postal services — critical for receiving deliveries and emergency services.

## How to read this data  
**FULL_ADDR** — The complete street address (e.g., "12924 JOSEPHINE ST").  
**COUNTY** — Two-letter county code (e.g., "SC" for Sarpy County).  
**ZIP** — The 5-digit postal code (e.g., "68505" for Lincoln).  
**LAT/LONG** — Geographic coordinates (e.g., 40.83235642, -96.6414176) used to map the location.  

## Try it yourself  
Verify your home or business address appears correctly by searching for your street name in the **ST_NAME** field (e.g., "JOSEPHINE") and checking the **FULL_ADDR** matches your expectation.

## What this tracks  
This dataset lists all airports in Nebraska, including their locations, facilities, and operational details.

## Why it matters to you  
If you're planning a business trip or shipping goods, this data helps you choose the nearest airport with the services you need—like jet fuel availability or runway lighting for night flights. Small aviation businesses can scout locations by comparing airport amenities, such as fixed-base operators (FBOs) or fuel types. For rural residents, it clarifies which nearby airports offer emergency medical flights or cargo services.

## How to read this data  
**Name** — Official airport name, like *Ainsworth Regional Airport*.  
**Code** — Three-letter airport identifier (e.g., *ANW* for Ainsworth).  
**Fuel** — Available fuel types, such as *100 LL & Jet A*.  
**Runway1** — Primary runway designation and orientation (e.g., *17 / 35* means runways align northeast/southwest).  

## Try it yourself  
Search the dataset for airports near your Nebraska town using the **City** field (e.g., "Ainsworth") to check runway surfaces or fuel options before booking a flight.

**PageNum** — The grid section number (e.g., "4"), corresponding to a physical map page in the ATLAS system.  
**PDF_MapURL** — If populated, this would link to a downloadable map of the grid section (sample shows blank values in this dataset).  
**Shape_Area** — The size of the grid section in square units (e.g., "7987348443.53"), useful for understanding the scale of each mapped area.  

## Try it yourself  
Visit the [Nebraska Game and Parks Commission ATLAS](https://outdoornebraska.gov/atlas/) and enter your county to see which grid section covers your preferred outdoor activity areas.

## Why it matters to you
